text: December fourth, eighteen seventy-two. In the middle of the Atlantic, a ship is sailing... with nobody on board.
The crew of the Dei Gratia spotted her drifting near the Azores.
She was the Mary Celeste, carrying seventeen hundred barrels of alcohol to Genoa.
Ten people should have been aboard. Captain Benjamin Briggs, his wife Sarah, their two-year-old Sophia, and seven crew.
The cargo was there. Plenty of food. Nothing stolen. Lowkey creepy.
But the lifeboat was gone, and so were the captain's papers and instruments.
The last log entry was nine days old. The ship had sailed on alone for about four hundred miles.
So why would a veteran captain put his family in a tiny boat, on the open ocean?
Maybe a pump failed, and he thought she was going down. Maybe the alcohol fumes scared them off. Or a waterspout hit.
And the warm meals left on the table? Pure eighteen-eighties fake news. A young Arthur Conan Doyle even turned it into fiction.
The ten people of the Mary Celeste were never seen again.
Only the ship came back... and she kept her secret.
